title: Exit code for CSV syntax errors
description: The sources list only ragged records under exit 3. An encoding/csv syntax error (for example a bare quote) could be exit 1 or exit 3. Chosen: 3, the nearest rejection code, with nothing on stdout.

title: Destination and exit status of --help
description: The sources define no help behavior. Chosen: usage text on standard output and exit 0.

title: Column name matching
description: Chosen: --column and --freq names match a trimmed header name exactly and case-sensitively.

title: Exact arithmetic
description: Sums, means, and medians use math/big (big.Int and big.Rat) and are rounded half away from zero only when written.
system_choice: math/big exact arithmetic, single rounding at output

title: Directory as input path
description: A path that is a directory, or any path that cannot be opened or read, exits 1 with nothing on standard output.

title: Byte handling
description: Input bytes are compared as bytes: a byte-order mark is not stripped and invalid UTF-8 is not rejected.

title: --top accepts digits only
description: Options were to accept a leading '+' or to accept digits only. I accept digits only, so '+5' is a usage error (exit 2). A value too large for int is treated as unbounded. Is that acceptable, or should '+5' be accepted?
